U11 / Atom.sit: You're the first forechecker (F1) chasing the puck into their zone. What's your main job?
opts: Pressure the puck carrier and steer where the puck can go
Hit the biggest defender as hard as possible
Stand in front of their net waiting for a turnover
Guard their bench so they can't change lines

U11 / Atom.tip: F1 steers the breakout into traffic.

U11 / Atom.sit: As F1, you approach the defender behind their net with the puck. Why take an angled path instead of a straight line?

The angle takes away one side, making their breakout predictable
Straight lines behind the net are against the rules
The angle hides you from the defender's view completely

U11 / Atom.tip: Angle in, take a side away.

media.alt: You are the defender, skating a curved path that steers the puck carrier toward the boards, your stick on the ice in their lane.

U11 / Atom.sit: You're forechecking alone — your linemates are still changing. The carrier has full control and support. Pressure hard or contain?
opts: Pressure hard anyway — effort always beats numbers
Contain — slow them down until your support arrives
Leave the zone and wait at your own blue line
Go for the biggest hit you can to spark the bench

U11 / Atom.tip: No support? Contain, don't chase.

Pressure hard now — a bobbled puck with support is green light
Stop and point at the bobble so your teammate can see it
Back off toward the slot in case they pass the puck there

U11 / Atom.tip: Bobble plus backup equals go.

The defender forgetting the breakout play they practiced

The player closest to the referee at the moment
Their biggest player, so they can't hit anyone

U11 / Atom.sit: Backchecking on a 3-on-2 against you, which attacker is the 'highest-threat option' you should hunt down?

The one skating slowest, since they're the easiest to catch
The one in the most dangerous ice, driving the middle lane
Whichever one is yelling for the puck the very loudest

U11 / Atom.tip: Chase the danger, not the easy catch.

U11 / Atom.sit: While backchecking, why do coaches tell you to skate WITH your check rather than just skating toward the puck?
opts: Skating with your check saves energy for offence
Chasing the puck leaves your check free behind you for the pass
The puck carrier is your defence partner's parent's favourite
Skating toward the puck is offside on the backcheck
U11 / Atom.why: Puck-chasing backcheckers get burned by one pass. Stay with your check, stick in their lane, and the carrier's best option skates in your pocket.
U11 / Atom.tip: Backcheck people, not pucks.

U11 / Atom.sit: You backcheck hard and catch up beside the trailing attacker just as the rush enters your zone. Where's your stick?
opts: In the passing lane between the puck and your check
Raised in the air to show the referee your effort
Hooked lightly on their hip to slow them down
Poking at the puck carrier way across the ice

U11 / Atom.tip: Catch up, then close the lane.

media.alt: The other team rushes toward your net. You backcheck through the middle of the ice, closing on the open attacker who drives the middle lane.

opts: Skating home through the middle, reading who to pick up
Skating along the boards where you can't be passed to
Following the exact path the puck carrier took up the ice
Yelling 'I'm back!' as you cross over each blue line

U11 / Atom.tip: Come home through the middle, eyes up.

Being angrier than the other player
Arriving second so you can see their move
Swinging your stick at the puck from far away

U11 / Atom.tip: Win the position, win the puck.

U11 / Atom.sit: You win a hard battle in the corner and come out with the puck. Why do coaches say the battle CREATED something?

Possession is the start of every read — now your team gets to decide
The other player must sit out one shift after losing a battle
Battles won count double in the final standings

U11 / Atom.tip: Battles buy the puck. Reads spend it.

Explaining to each teammate what went wrong out there
Next play — skate your next shift hard like the mistake is gone
Asking the coach to sit you for the rest of the period

No, because loose pucks legally belong to the home team

U11 / Atom.sit: You're tangled in a net-front battle when the puck pops loose beside you. What separates good battlers here?

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck and your teammate is skating up the middle with no one near them. A defender is reaching for you. What is the best play?

Hold onto it and try to skate around the defender
Shoot it all the way down the ice
Stop and wait for help

U9 / Novice.sit: You carry the puck into the corner, down near the net you are attacking. A teammate is standing alone right in front of the net. A defender is skating toward you. What is the best play?
opts: Fire a shot at the net from where you stand
Skate back toward the middle of the ice with the puck
Send a pass to your teammate for a close-range chance
Wait near the boards until more room opens up

U9 / Novice.sit: You are in the middle of the ice. You see two players from the other team racing toward your end, and they are ahead of all your teammates. What does this tell you is most likely about to happen?
opts: The other team will lose the puck on their own
Your team will recover before the rush hits
A scoring chance is developing against your team
Your goalie can stop the play without help
U9 / Novice.explain: When two players from the other team are ahead of all your teammates, that is a sign a dangerous rush is heading toward your end. Spotting that pattern early gives your whole team a chance to get back and protect your goalie.

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck on the side boards deep in the end you are attacking. A teammate is standing right in front of the net with no defender nearby. What is the best play?
opts: Shoot at the goalie from your spot on the boards
Carry the puck toward the net for a closer shot
Hold onto the puck and try to stickhandle through
Pass the puck to the teammate waiting at the net
U9 / Novice.explain: Your teammate is already set up at the front of the net with nobody around them, which is the best spot to score from. A quick pass gets the puck there right away, giving your team a much better chance than shooting from the tough side-boards angle.

U9 / Novice.sit: Your teammate has the puck near the boards and is about to send you a pass on the wing. You have a second before it arrives. What should you do in that moment?
opts: Keep your eyes on the puck as it comes
Turn your head to check who is near you
Skate toward your teammate to shorten the pass
Call out to show your teammate you are open
U9 / Novice.explain: The moment before the puck arrives is your best chance to see who is nearby. Watching only the puck while it travels is tempting, but once it hits your stick the chance to look is gone, so a quick check now gives you a head start on your next play.

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck in the corner near the net. A defender is skating toward you quickly. Your teammate is standing all alone at the front of the net. What is the best play?
opts: Try to skate past the defender with the puck
Pass to your teammate at the front of the net
Skate back up the ice to find more space
Shoot the puck toward the net from the corner
U9 / Novice.explain: Your teammate at the front of the net is in a great spot to score. From the corner, the net is hard to hit cleanly, but your teammate has a clear look at it.

U9 / Novice.sit: Your teammate is about to pass you the puck in the middle of the ice. What is the best thing to do in the moment before the puck arrives?
opts: Skate straight toward the opponent's net to get into position
Wait until the puck arrives to plan your next move
Keep both eyes locked on the puck coming your way
Take a quick look around to spot who is open
U9 / Novice.explain: That moment before the puck arrives is your chance to look around, so you already know where to go the instant you catch it. If you stare at the puck instead, you will have no plan ready when it lands on your stick.

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck at the top of the circles in the end you are attacking. Your teammate is standing alone near the front of the net, with no defender close by. The goalie is set in the crease watching you. What is the best play?
opts: Take a shot from the top of the circles
Skate the puck back away from the net
Carry the puck into the near corner
Pass to your teammate near the front of the net
U9 / Novice.explain: Your teammate near the front of the net is open and in a much better scoring spot. The goalie is already set and watching you, so sending the puck to your close, open teammate gives your team a better chance to score than shooting from farther away.

U9 / Novice.sit: Your teammate shoots, and the puck bounces off the goalie's pads out in front of the net. The goalie is down, and a defender is starting toward the loose puck. What is the best play?

Stop near the net and tap the loose puck quickly before the defender gets there
Peel away toward the boards to look for a pass
Wait for your teammate to skate in for their own rebound

U9 / Novice.sit: When you are defending a 2-on-1 rush, you should always chase straight at the player with the puck and reach for it.
U9 / Novice.why: If you chase only the puck carrier, they can pass to the open teammate. A U9 defender should protect the middle and try to take away the dangerous pass.

U9 / Novice.sit: A player is standing by the boards waiting for a pass. The puck is passed, but it hits a skate and bounces into open ice. The player stays on the boards and waits.

They stood still instead of reading the bounce and skating to the open ice to get the puck
They should have backed up toward their own end before going after the puck
They moved their stick blade on the ice too early
U9 / Novice.explain: Pucks do not always come straight to your stick. Reading the play means reacting when the puck changes direction and skating to the loose puck first.

U9 / Novice.sit: You are skating up the ice, and a teammate with the puck is skating right beside you. A defender steps up to block your teammate.
opts: Slow down beside your teammate and wait for them to beat the defender
Skate directly behind your teammate and hope for a drop pass in the same traffic
Skate away from the defender into an open lane so your teammate has a clear pass
Cut in front of your teammate and skate toward the puck
U9 / Novice.explain: When the defender steps up to your teammate, open ice appears beside or behind that pressure. Moving into that lane gives your teammate a simple pass option.

U9 / Novice.sit: Your defender has the puck behind your net, looking to pass it up the ice to you. The other team's winger is standing right between you and your defender. What is the best play?
opts: Stay exactly where you are and tap your stick on the ice
Skate to an open pocket of ice where the winger is not blocking the pass
Skate closer to the boards where the winger is already blocking the lane
Turn up ice without looking back for the puck

U9 / Novice.sit: You are leading a 2-on-1 rush toward the net. The only defender slides over to block your pass, leaving you a clear path to the goalie. What is the best play?
opts: Try to force a pass through the defender's skates to your teammate anyway
Slow down and wait for the defender to choose again
Skate toward the net and take a quick shot yourself
Dump the puck into the corner even though you have a shooting lane

U9 / Novice.sit: A player receives a pass near the other team's net. The goalie is out of position, and no defender is between the player and the open net. The player passes the puck back to a teammate far from the net.

They should have waited longer to see if a defender would arrive
They should have skated behind the net to keep the puck safe
They should have passed into the corner before looking at the net

U9 / Novice.sit: You pick up the puck in your defensive corner. You look up the boards and see a defender waiting there to pressure you.

Stop, turn back, and skate behind your own net to use the open ice on the other side
Force the puck up the boards straight into the defender
Throw a blind pass through the middle of your end

U9 / Novice.tip: Use the open side of the ice.

U9 / Novice.sit: Your teammate is battling for the puck on the boards. You are open in front of the net. The puck pops right to you. What is the best play?

Pass the puck back into the pile of players on the boards
Stickhandle toward the boards to make a safer play
Stop and wait for the goalie to get set

U9 / Novice.sit: You are carrying the puck up the ice and see three defenders waiting in front of you. Your teammate is skating fast into open ice on the outside wing. What is the best play?

Pass the puck to your teammate in the open space before you reach the defenders
Slow down and wait until a defender comes closer
Turn around and skate all the way back to your own net

U9 / Novice.sit: If a defender is chasing you in open ice, gliding with both feet still is the best way to keep your space.

U9 / Novice.sit: A player has the puck and open ice in front of them. No defender is close, but they panic and slap the puck down the ice to no one.

They gave the puck away instead of carrying it into the open space
They should have passed backward right away even with open ice ahead
They should have taken a big shot from far away

U9 / Novice.sit: You are on defence in your own end. The puck comes to you, and you have plenty of time and space. No forechecker is near you.

Keep your head up, skate forward into space, and make a good pass
Stand still with the puck until a forechecker arrives
Throw a blind pass through the middle of your end

U9 / Novice.sit: Your teammate wins a faceoff in the end you are attacking. The puck slides back to you, and you have a clear lane to the net. What is the best play?

Take a quick step into the open lane and shoot before the space closes
Pass to a covered teammate along the boards
Skate all the way into the corner with the puck

U9 / Novice.sit: You get the puck behind the other team's net. A defender chases you around the right side and cuts off your path. What is the best play?

Throw the puck to the front of the net without looking
Freeze behind the net and wait for the defender to take the puck

U9 / Novice.sit: If a defender's stick blocks the direct pass and your teammate is near the boards, banking the puck softly off the boards can be a creative way to pass.
U9 / Novice.why: The boards can help you move the puck around a defender's stick. At U9, a soft bank pass is a simple creative play when the direct lane is blocked.

U9 / Novice.sit: A player is stuck in the corner with a defender reaching for the puck. Instead of turning their body to protect it, they face the defender directly and try to stickhandle.

They should have passed blindly through the middle right away
They should have shot from the corner before protecting the puck
They should have stopped moving their feet completely
U9 / Novice.explain: Under pressure, your body can protect the puck. Turning sideways or away from the defender keeps the puck safer and gives you time to find help.

U9 / Novice.sit: You are skating up the wing, and a defender steps up right in front of you. Your teammate is skating into open ice behind the defender.

Chip the puck softly off the boards into space for your teammate
Stop and wait for the defender to take the puck
Turn all the way back without looking for your teammate

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck in front of the net, ready to shoot, but a defender drops down in front of you to block the lane. What is the best play?

Fake the shot, pull the puck to the side, and take a quick shot around the blocker
Skate backward out of the front of the net right away
Pass to a covered teammate behind you

U9 / Novice.sit: The best play is to put your head down and stickhandle straight through all three defenders.

U9 / Novice.sit: On a 2-on-1, the defender should skate straight at the puck carrier and leave the other attacker open.
U9 / Novice.why: If the defender chases only the puck, the pass across is open. Staying between the two attackers helps block the dangerous pass.

Stop and wait for help

Steer your skates toward the open left side and keep your feet moving
Shoot the puck down the ice before the defenders get closer

U7 / Initiation.sit: You are down at the end you are attacking, trying to score, but a player on the other team steals the puck and starts skating fast toward your goalie. What is the best play?

Stay near the other team's net in case your team steals it back
Glide slowly toward your own end and watch where the puck goes
Stop, turn around, and skate hard back toward your own net to help your goalie

U7 / Initiation.sit: Your teammate is skating down the wing with the puck and is about to shoot on the goalie. You are skating down the middle of the ice. What is the best play?
opts: Skate into the corner in case the shot misses the net
Stop near the front or side of the net with your stick on the ice, ready for a rebound
Skate up beside your teammate and call for the puck right away
Stop high in the zone and watch the shot

U7 / Initiation.sit: A player digs the puck out of the corner right next to their own goalie. They decide to skate the puck directly across the front of their own net to get to the other side.

They did not skate fast enough while crossing in front of the goalie
They should have stopped behind the net and waited for everyone to leave
They should have passed through the middle to a teammate right away
U7 / Initiation.explain: The front of your own net is a dangerous place to lose the puck. A safer U7 habit is to turn up the boards or use the wall instead of carrying the puck across the scoring area.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You are stickhandling up the ice, but you accidentally lose the puck off the toe of your blade. It is sitting just a few feet away from you.

Stop, pivot, and get right back on the puck before anyone else can reach it
Slow down and wait for a teammate to pick it up
Look down at your stick before you chase the puck

U7 / Initiation.tip: Take a quick look before you touch the puck.
U7 / Initiation.why: A quick peek over your shoulder helps you see pressure and open ice. Then you can pick up the puck and skate to safety.

U7 / Initiation.sit: Your teammate intercepts a pass and has a clear breakaway. They are skating as fast as they can toward the other team's net. What is the best play?
opts: Coast in the middle and watch the shot
Turn toward the bench because the play is far away
Stop partway and watch so you do not get too close
Skate hard behind them to follow up on the play
U7 / Initiation.explain: A breakaway can still create a rebound or loose puck. Following the play hard puts you close enough to help if the goalie makes the save.

U7 / Initiation.sit: A player on the other team has the puck directly behind your net. You are the only defender back. What is the best play?
opts: Stay in front of your goalie with your stick on the ice to protect the scoring area
Chase the player all the way behind the net to try to steal the puck
Stand beside one post and only watch the puck carrier
Skate toward the corner boards before the puck carrier comes out
U7 / Initiation.explain: A player behind the net is most dangerous when they pass or skate out front. Staying in the scoring area helps you protect your goalie and the middle of the ice.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You are standing in open ice. Your teammate has the puck and looks right at you. You want them to pass it. What is the best play?
opts: Yell loudly while your stick blade is off the ice
Hold your stick near your skates without showing a clear target
Turn away and skate into space where they cannot see your stick
Tap your stick blade flat on the ice where you want the puck
U7 / Initiation.explain: A good pass needs a clear target. Put your blade flat on the ice so your teammate knows where to send the puck and you are ready to catch it.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You shoot the puck, and the goalie catches it in their glove. The referee blows the whistle. What should you do?
opts: Keep skating in and try to poke the puck loose before the goalie covers it
Stop right away, turn away from the goalie, and get ready for the next play
Skate through the crease to see if the puck falls out
Stand beside the goalie and wait for the referee to drop the puck there
U7 / Initiation.explain: The whistle means the play is stopped. Good players stop right away, respect the goalie, and get ready for the next faceoff.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You skate into the end you are attacking and see that two of your teammates are already in the right corner trying to get the puck from a defender.
opts: Skate into the right corner to make it three teammates near the same puck
Skate all the way back all the way back to your own end
Skate to the front of the net or the open left side and get your stick ready
Stand right behind your two teammates in the corner
U7 / Initiation.explain: If two teammates are already near the puck, they need a passing option more than another player in the same space. Find open ice and be ready when they win it.

U7 / Initiation.sit: The other team is attacking, but your goalie makes a save and the puck goes out to your defender. What is the best play?
opts: Turn up the ice, start skating forward, and look back for a pass
Stay in front of your goalie in case the puck comes back
Skate slowly sideways and wait for your defender to carry it
Skate into the same corner as your defender
U7 / Initiation.explain: When your team gets the puck, you can help start offence. Skate up ice with your stick ready so your defender has a forward passing option.

U7 / Initiation.sit: An attacker is skating fast right at you with the puck. You are the last defender back. What is the best play?
opts: Reach only for the puck and let your body drift to one side
Keep your body between the attacker and your net, steering them toward the boards
Back straight into your goalie so you do not get beaten
Skate straight at the attacker and guess which way they will go
U7 / Initiation.explain: The last defender should protect the middle first. Keep your body between the puck carrier and your net, then guide them toward the boards where the shot is harder.

U7 / Initiation.sit: When you are guarding a player without the puck in front of your net, you should hold your stick high in the air so you are ready to bat the puck if it pops up.
U7 / Initiation.tip: Keep your stick on the ice in the passing lane.
U7 / Initiation.why: Most dangerous passes near the net travel along the ice. A stick on the ice can block the pass before it reaches the player you are guarding.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You get a great pass in the middle of the ice. The only person between you and the goal is the goalie. What is the best play?
opts: Stop skating right away so you can take a big shot from far away
Pass the puck backward even though you have open ice
Skate wide into the corner to stay away from pressure
Keep your feet moving, skate toward the net, and shoot
U7 / Initiation.explain: When you have open ice in front of you, keep skating. Moving your feet gets you closer to the net and gives you a better chance to score.

U7 / Initiation.sit: Your goalie saves the puck to the corner. Two players from the other team skate toward it. You are the closest defender to your net. What is the best play?
opts: Skate to the front of your net and keep your stick on the ice
Chase both attackers deep into the corner
Stand behind your own net and wait
Skate up the ice looking for a pass
U7 / Initiation.explain: The puck is in the corner, but the dangerous place is in front of your goalie. At U7, the simple read is to protect the net first.

U7 / Initiation.sit: If a player on the other team has the puck behind your net, you should chase them around the back and leave the front of the net open.
U7 / Initiation.why: They cannot score from behind the net. Stay near the front so you can stop a pass or loose puck by your goalie.

U7 / Initiation.sit: Your teammate is skating down the side and is about to shoot. You are skating down the middle.
opts: Skate into the corner in case the puck misses
Stop near the side of the net with your stick on the ice for a rebound
Skate up to your teammate and crowd the puck
Stop high in the zone and watch
U7 / Initiation.explain: Shots often bounce off the goalie. If you stop near the net with your stick ready, you can be first to the rebound.

U7 / Initiation.sit: The other team steals the puck and skates fast toward your net. A defender stops in the middle of the ice and watches them go by.
U7 / Initiation.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They stopped skating instead of coming back to help protect their net
They should have chased from behind with only their stick
They should have waited up the ice for a pass
They should have stayed near the other team's net
U7 / Initiation.explain: When the other team gets the puck, your job changes to defence. Skate back hard and help your goalie.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You are standing in front of the other team's net. Your teammate has the puck in the corner and looks at you. What is the best play?
opts: Wave your hands while your stick is off the ice
Skate right up to your teammate and bring traffic with you
Keep your stick blade flat on the ice as a target
Turn your back and skate away from the net
U7 / Initiation.explain: A good pass needs a clear target. Keeping your stick on the ice shows where the puck should go and gets you ready to shoot.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You are skating down the ice with the puck. A defender is standing still in front of you. The side of the ice is empty. What is the best play?
opts: Put your head down and skate straight at the defender
Stop moving and wait for them to move away
Steer to the empty side and skate past them
Shoot the puck from far away before you get closer
U7 / Initiation.explain: When someone blocks your path, look for open ice. Steering to the empty side is safer than skating into traffic.

U7 / Initiation.sit: When you hear the referee blow the whistle, you should keep playing just in case the puck goes in.
U7 / Initiation.why: The whistle means the play is stopped. Good players stop right away and get ready for the next play.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You dig the puck out of the corner beside your own goalie. A defender is standing in front of your net.
opts: Skate the puck up the boards, keeping it close to the wall
Skate the puck right across the front of your own net
Leave the puck in the corner and skate away
Pass it backward toward your own goalie
U7 / Initiation.explain: The front of your own net is dangerous. The boards are the safer path when you are leaving your end.

U7 / Initiation.sit: A player gets a pass in the middle of the ice. Only the goalie is between them and the net. They pass the puck backward right away.
U7 / Initiation.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They should have shot from farther away
They passed instead of skating toward the net to shoot
They should have skated into the corner to be safe
They should have waited until a defender caught them
U7 / Initiation.explain: When you have open ice and a chance to score, keep your feet moving toward the net and shoot.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You are on a breakaway with only the goalie in front of you. A player from the other team is skating hard behind you. What is the best play?
opts: Stop skating and let them catch up
Keep skating fast toward the net and shoot
Turn around and skate back toward the player chasing you
Shoot the puck into the corner and chase it
U7 / Initiation.explain: On a breakaway, speed helps you stay ahead. Keep your feet moving and go to the net.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You get the puck near the boards down in your own end. A player from the other team skates at you. The ice along the wall is open. What is the best play?
opts: Keep your feet moving and skate up the boards into open ice
Stop skating and hide the puck between your skates
Pass across the front of your own net
Stand still and wait for help
U7 / Initiation.explain: Open ice helps you escape. Keep moving into the space instead of stopping where pressure can catch you.

U7 / Initiation.sit: If two of your teammates are already in the corner battling for the puck, you should skate into the same corner and stand beside them.
U7 / Initiation.why: If two teammates are already near the puck, they need someone open. Move to space so they have a pass.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You are skating with the puck, but it slips off your stick. It is only a few feet away.
opts: Keep skating in a big circle to come back for it
Give up and let the other team have it
Look at your stick before chasing the puck
Stop, turn, and get back on the puck
U7 / Initiation.explain: Everyone loses the puck sometimes. Stop and turn right away so you can win it back.

U7 / Initiation.sit: Your teammate has the puck on the boards. Two defenders are poking at them. You skate right up next to your teammate and stand still.
U7 / Initiation.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They joined the crowd instead of finding open ice
They should have poked the puck away from their teammate
They should have hidden behind the other team's net
They should have skated back to their own goalie
U7 / Initiation.explain: If you stand in the same crowd, your teammate has no easy pass. Move to open ice and show your stick.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You pick up a loose puck in the middle of the ice. Nobody is between you and the other team's goalie. What is the best play?
opts: Pass to a teammate who is covered
Carry the puck toward the net as fast as you can
Skate backward with the puck
Shoot from way out instead of skating closer
U7 / Initiation.explain: When you have open ice, use it. Carrying the puck closer gives you a better chance to score.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You are in the corner with the puck. A defender's stick blocks the direct pass, and your teammate is open nearby. What is the best play?
opts: Bank the puck softly off the boards to your teammate
Try to chop the puck through the defender's stick
Cover the puck with your hand
Shoot the puck high at the glass
U7 / Initiation.explain: The boards can help you pass around a stick. A soft bank pass can reach your teammate when the straight pass is blocked.

U7 / Initiation.sit: When a defender follows you around the back of the net, stopping and going back the other way can help you find open ice.
U7 / Initiation.tip: Use the net as a shield.
U7 / Initiation.why: The net can block the defender's path. A quick stop and turn can help you skate out the open side.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You have the puck near your goal line. A forechecker is coming to trap you on the wall.
opts: Force the puck straight up the wall into pressure
Throw the puck blindly to the front of your own net
Fake up the boards, turn back, and skate behind your net
Stop on the wall and wait
U7 / Initiation.explain: A simple fake can make space. Show one way, then turn to the open ice behind your net.
U7 / Initiation.tip: Fake one way, go the other.

U7 / Initiation.sit: A player picks up a loose puck in their own end. A forechecker skates toward them, and the player smacks the puck into a crowded corner.
U7 / Initiation.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They panicked and threw the puck away instead of skating to open ice
They should have passed through the forechecker's skates
They should have skated into their goalie
They should have shot from their own end
U7 / Initiation.explain: When pressure comes, do not throw the puck away. Use your feet to turn toward open ice and keep the puck safer.

U7 / Initiation.sit: A defender slides on the ice in front of you to block your shot. What is the best play?
opts: Shoot right into the defender's pads
Pull the puck around them and shoot through the open lane
Pass backward right away even though you can shoot
Leave the puck and skate away
U7 / Initiation.explain: When a defender slides down, they cannot turn quickly. Pull the puck around them and use the open lane.

U7 / Initiation.sit: The defender should chase the puck carrier behind the net and leave the front of the net open.
U7 / Initiation.why: A player behind the net cannot shoot straight in. The dangerous space is in front of the goalie, so the defender should protect that area first.

U7 / Initiation.sit: Stopping your feet is the best way to escape a defender.
U7 / Initiation.why: Open ice helps you escape. If you stop, the defender can close the space, so keep skating into the open lane.

U13 / Peewee.sit: 3-on-2 rush. You are the middle driver without the puck. The puck carrier is wide on the right. What should you do?
opts: Drive hard to the net for a pass or rebound
Curl back toward the blue line
Stop at the top of the circles and wait
Skate to the same side as the puck carrier
U13 / Peewee.explain: On a 3-on-2 the middle lane drives the net — it forces the defence to honour you and opens a pass or a rebound. Spreading the attack stretches two defenders across three lanes.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are the lone defender on a 2-on-1. The puck carrier is winding up to shoot. What is your job?
opts: Take away the pass and let your goalie have the shot
Slide to block the shot and leave the pass open
Skate at the puck carrier to try a poke check
Back all the way in to the net
U13 / Peewee.explain: On a 2-on-1 the defender takes away the pass and trusts the goalie to handle the shot. A shooter the goalie can see is a better outcome than a back-door tap-in.

U13 / Peewee.sit: Your defender is about to send you a breakout pass in your own zone. Your eyes have been on the puck since the play started, so you have no idea where the nearest opposing player is. The puck is about two seconds away from reaching you. What is the most important thing to do right now?
opts: Skate into open ice to put distance between yourself and any defender
Let your defender know you are ready by calling out to them
Do a quick shoulder check to spot pressure and find open teammates
Keep your eyes on the puck to make sure you receive it cleanly
U13 / Peewee.explain: Before the puck arrives is your last chance to collect information, so a quick shoulder check tells you where pressure is coming from and which teammates are open. If you catch the puck without that read, you will be reacting to what you find instead of already knowing your best option.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are the right wing in the neutral zone. Your teammate has the puck and is about to pass it your way. A defender is nearby, watching you closely. You just found open space. What is the most important thing to do before the puck arrives?
opts: Signal your teammate to hold the pass for a moment
Keep both eyes on the puck so you don't miss the catch
Position your body toward the boards for puck protection
Take a quick look around to see where the pressure is
U13 / Peewee.explain: A quick look around before the puck reaches you tells you exactly where that defender is, so you already have a plan the moment you catch it. Watching the puck, signaling a hold, or pre-positioning your body all leave you blind to that defender's location when the puck lands.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You have the puck on the half-wall in the offensive zone. The goalie is set and ready to stop a shot from where you are standing. Your teammate is open in the high-danger area right in front of the net, with no defender close enough to challenge them. A defender is closing toward you. What is the best play?
opts: Skate across the zone to get a better shooting angle
Carry the puck in toward the net yourself
Send it to your teammate in front right away
Shoot from your current spot on the wall
U13 / Peewee.explain: Your teammate is standing in the high-danger area with no one near them, so a quick pass gives them a clean shot before any defender arrives. A shot from the wall is low-percentage here because the goalie is already in position to cover it.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are bringing the puck up the ice through the neutral zone on a rush. You see the first layer of defence stepping up on you. Why is it critical to scan the second layer behind them?
opts: To know if you can chip the puck into space and retrieve it behind the first defender
To see if the far winger is open before you decide whether the chip is safe
To decide if you should slow down and wait for a trailer behind you
So you can immediately turn back and reset the breakout the moment you spot a second defender
U13 / Peewee.explain: Scanning beyond the first defender tells you whether there is usable space behind pressure. If the second layer is too close, a chip can become a turnover. If there is space, an area play can let you keep speed.

U13 / Peewee.sit: When playing weak-side wing in the defensive zone, it is best to stay locked onto the puck so you never lose track of the play.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Scan between the puck and your check.
U13 / Peewee.why: If you stare only at the puck, you can lose the weak-side threat in the slot or at the point. A U13 winger should keep switching their eyes between the puck, open opponents, and their coverage job.

U13 / Peewee.sit: A defender receives a D-to-D pass in the neutral zone. They look down to catch it cleanly, hold onto it for three seconds while looking for a pass, and get pressured by the forechecker.
U13 / Peewee.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They called for the pass while standing still instead of building speed
They failed to scan up the ice before the pass arrived, resulting in slow decision making
They should have reversed the puck back to their partner immediately
They held the puck in the middle lane instead of moving it toward the boards
U13 / Peewee.explain: Pre-scanning lets the defender know the next option before the puck arrives. Without that early look, they spend too long processing after the catch and give the forechecker time to close.

U13 / Peewee.sit: Your team is cycling the puck low in the offensive zone. You are the high forward (F3). You scan the slot and see it is open.
opts: Back all the way out toward the red line to protect against a turnover
Slide into the open high slot, show your stick, and stay ready to recover if possession changes
Skate down below the goal line to make it a three-player puck battle
Stay wide near the boards and wait for a rim or rebound
U13 / Peewee.explain: F3 can become a scoring option when quiet ice opens, but they still need defensive awareness. Sliding into the high slot with a target gives the puck carrier an option without abandoning responsibility above the puck.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Find quiet ice without giving up your safety role.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are a winger slashing across the neutral zone to receive a breakout pass. Order the steps for a successful entry.
items: Catch the puck in stride while maintaining your speed
Scan the offensive blue line to locate the defenders' gap
Use the gap read to decide whether to carry, chip, or pass
Present a clear target with your stick to your passing defender
U13 / Peewee.explain: The winger should read the gap before asking for the puck. Catching in stride matters, and the earlier scan helps the player choose the entry before the defence can close.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are a defender defending a 2-on-1 rush. What should your eyes be doing as the play crosses your blue line?
opts: Lock only on the puck carrier and angle hard toward them
Look mostly at the puck so you are ready to block the shot
Quickly shifting focus back and forth between the puck carrier and the dangerous pass option
Watch the puck carrier's skates so you can time a poke check
U13 / Peewee.explain: On a 2-on-1, the defender must manage both threats. Scanning between the puck carrier and the passing option helps you protect the middle, take away the most dangerous pass, and avoid chasing one player too early.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You pick up a loose puck in the high slot of your defensive zone. You feel pressure right on your back, but you have not scanned up the ice yet.
opts: Chip a backhand pass toward the middle and hope a teammate is there
Protect the puck with your body and skate toward the safer boards to buy time to look up
Turn back into the slot to keep possession in the middle of the ice
Rim the puck hard around the boards before checking where your winger is
U13 / Peewee.explain: In the defensive high slot, a blind play through the middle is dangerous. If you have pressure and no scan, protect the puck first, move toward safer ice, and get your eyes up before choosing the next play.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Protect first, then scan and move the puck.

U13 / Peewee.sit: A good habit for a centre on a faceoff win in the offensive zone is to immediately look back at their own defender to make sure the puck was caught cleanly.
U13 / Peewee.tip: After the win, scan opponents and get to your job.
U13 / Peewee.why: Once the puck is won back, the centre should quickly find their check, tie up pressure when needed, and get to the net-front or slot area for a screen, tip, or loose puck instead of watching the defender.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are the gold puck carrier on this odd-man rush. The navy defender has taken away the pass to your teammate in the middle. What is your best option?
opts: Shoot the puck using the clear lane the defender gave you
Try to force a pass through the navy defender to the middle teammate
Stop and wait for the navy defender to move away
Carry toward the corner even though the shooting lane is open
U13 / Peewee.explain: When the defender takes away the pass on an odd-man rush, the shot lane is open. Take the ice they give you and put the puck on net.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are the gold puck carrier on an odd-man rush. The navy defender is backing in and giving you a lot of open ice. What should you do first?
opts: Carry the puck into the open space to force the defender to make a choice
Shoot from far away before using the open ice
Throw a blind pass across before the defender commits
Turn toward the boards and shield the puck
U13 / Peewee.explain: If the defender gives you space, use it. Carrying forward improves your shot and can force the defender to open a pass later.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You have the puck in the middle on an odd-man rush. The navy defender shifts toward your gold teammate on the left. Who has the best open ice?
opts: The gold teammate open on the right side
The gold teammate covered on the left side
The small space directly behind the navy defender
The corner behind the navy goalie
U13 / Peewee.explain: The navy defender cannot cover both sides. When they shade toward the left-side teammate, move the puck to the open gold teammate on the right.

opts: The trailing gold forward open in the high slot
The gold centre driving into tight coverage near the net
The narrow lane between the navy defender and the boards
The far corner away from the scoring area

U13 / Peewee.sit: As a defender backing up on a 1-on-1, you should match the attacker's speed early but stay three stick lengths away all the way into the top of the circles.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Match speed early, then tighten the gap.
U13 / Peewee.why: Matching speed is useful, but staying too far away near dangerous ice gives the attacker room to shoot, cut back, or pass. At U13, the defender should close the gap with feet and stick before the rush reaches the prime scoring area.

U13 / Peewee.sit: The puck turns over in the neutral zone. The defender immediately backs all the way to the top of their crease, leaving the blue line and neutral-zone ice uncontested.
U13 / Peewee.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They retreated too far and gave the attacker free ice to build speed
They pivoted backward even though defenders should always sprint forward
They stayed inside the dots instead of chasing the puck to the boards right away
They kept their stick in the lane instead of swinging it at the puck
U13 / Peewee.explain: The mistake is not backing up by itself. The mistake is giving up too much ice. A good U13 defender surfs backward with control, holds a useful gap near the blue line, and steers the rush before it reaches the slot.

U13 / Peewee.sit: Your winger is driving the puck wide down the right side. You are the centre arriving late. The weak-side defender is locked onto the puck carrier and has not checked behind them.
opts: Drive hard to the far post to occupy the defender and create a second threat
Skate directly toward the puck carrier and crowd their lane
Stop at the blue line for a drop pass while the rush moves below you
Circle behind the net before the puck carrier has beaten the defender
U13 / Peewee.explain: The far-post drive gives the puck carrier a dangerous target and forces the weak-side defender to turn. That can open a pass to the net or space for the trailing player behind you.

U13 / Peewee.sit: When angling a fast skater toward the boards, the best route is a straight line at their chest, even if that opens the middle behind you.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Angle inside out, not straight at them.
U13 / Peewee.why: A straight line can miss the angle and let a fast player cut back or chip behind you. A curved inside-out route lets you match speed, protect the middle, and steer them toward the boards.

U13 / Peewee.sit: The opposing winger is skating up the boards. The defender has a good angle to the wall, but their stick is tucked near their own waist instead of taking away the puck-side lane.
U13 / Peewee.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They are not leading with their stick to take away the puck lane and inside pass
They are skating the attacker toward the boards instead of letting them cut middle
They are keeping their body inside the attacker instead of chasing from behind
They are matching speed instead of stopping to make the attacker slow down
U13 / Peewee.explain: A good angle needs an active stick. Leading with the stick helps block the pass or touch to the middle while the body steers the attacker toward lower-danger ice.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You intercept a pass in the neutral zone. Two opponents are closing from the middle, but your winger is already moving up the wide lane with open ice.
opts: Make a quick, firm pass to the winger who has speed and space
Try to split the two middle defenders before they close their sticks
Dump the puck in before checking whether the wide lane is open
Turn back toward your own zone and let the counterattack slow down
U13 / Peewee.explain: The middle is closing, but the wide lane is open. Moving the puck quickly to the player with speed creates a counterattack before the defenders can reset.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Use the open lane before it closes.

U13 / Peewee.sit: The other team misses the net, and the puck rims hard around the boards to you. You are starting a quick transition out of your zone. Put these steps in the right order.
items: Move your feet and snap a firm pass to the centre's tape.
Shoulder check before the puck arrives to read wall pressure.
Cushion the puck off the boards so you have control.
Locate your centre curling low as the first support option.
U13 / Peewee.explain: The read starts before the puck arrives. Check pressure, find your support, control the rimmed puck, then move it quickly while your feet are alive.

U13 / Peewee.sit: When protecting the puck in the corner, standing still and reaching with your arms is usually safer than using your feet and edges to change the defender's angle.
U13 / Peewee.why: A still puck carrier is easy to pin. Cutbacks, tight turns, and active feet help keep your body between the defender and the puck.

U13 / Peewee.sit: A forward carries the puck out of the corner. A defender closes from the forward's right side, but the forward keeps the puck exposed in front of their skates.
U13 / Peewee.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They failed to move the puck to the away hip and put their body between pressure and puck
They kept moving their feet instead of stopping to shield with only their arms
They stayed near the wall instead of cutting straight into the defender's stick
They looked up ice before the defender was fully beaten
U13 / Peewee.explain: When pressure comes from one side, move the puck to the away hip and use your legs and hips as the shield. That makes the defender reach through your body to get the puck.

U15 / Bantam.sit: You are the right winger in the offensive zone. The other team's left defender blocks a shot and moves to the puck in the corner. Their centre is already sprinting toward the boards on your side of the ice. Your own centre has pinched in at the far circle. What should you do right now?
opts: Crash the net in case the defender loses the puck
Move toward their centre to take away the boards
Back off to your own blue line to defend
Set up at the front of the net to screen
U15 / Bantam.explain: Their centre racing to the boards signals the outlet is forming, and with your own centre pinched deep, pressing them now is the only way to stop a clean breakout before the puck even moves. Crashing the net or screening only works when your team controls the puck, and drifting back first gives the other team a free pass out of their zone before your defence can set.

U15 / Bantam.sit: In defensive-zone coverage, if the opposing centre cycles high and switches spots with their defender, the covering forward should chase that centre all the way to the blue line without communicating.
U15 / Bantam.why: Blindly chasing a high cycle can pull coverage apart and open the slot. At U15 speed, players usually need to communicate a switch so the defensive shape stays layered and compact.

U15 / Bantam.sit: The opponent's puck carrier is tied up with your defenceman in the corner. The opposing centre slides into the slot, but your centre is puck-watching from the faceoff dot.
U15 / Bantam.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: Your centre lost defensive-side positioning on the most dangerous slot threat
Your centre should join the corner battle and leave the slot to the weak-side winger
Your centre should drift to the blue line early to prepare for a breakout
Your centre is too low even though the slot player is below the hash marks
U15 / Bantam.explain: The most dangerous player is often away from the puck in the high-danger area. Your centre has to shoulder check, locate the slot threat, and stay between that player and the net.

U15 / Bantam.sit: You are attacking 1-on-1 off the rush. The defender has a tight gap and is matching your speed in the middle, but the outside lane is open.
opts: Change pace with a hesitation, then accelerate into the wide lane
Force a toe drag through the defender's stick and skates in the middle
Stop completely and wait for the defender to back away on their own
Shoot from the blue line even though the defender is set in the lane
U15 / Bantam.explain: When the defender owns a tight middle gap, you have to disrupt their timing. A pace change can freeze their feet, then your acceleration attacks the open outside lane.
U15 / Bantam.tip: Change speed to change the gap.

U15 / Bantam.sit: You are a forward receiving an outlet pass and preparing to attack a lone defender on a 1-on-1 rush. Put these steps in the right order.
items: Push the puck slightly wide to make the defender turn their hips.
Build speed as you receive and move through the neutral zone.
Cut back hard to the middle once the defender leans outside.
Scan the defender's gap, stick, and feet before choosing your lane.
U15 / Bantam.explain: Speed makes the defender respect the rush. Then read their gap and feet, push wide to make them commit, and cut back only after they lean outside.

U15 / Bantam.sit: When backchecking against a fast rush, you should go straight to the puck carrier even if two teammates are already pressuring that player.
U15 / Bantam.tip: Sort the threats behind the puck.
U15 / Bantam.why: If teammates already have the puck carrier, another player chasing the puck can leave the trailer or weak-side attacker open. At U15, the backchecker must scan and pick up the next most dangerous option.

U15 / Bantam.sit: You are a defender retrieving a dump-in. The forechecker takes an inside angle and cuts off your partner. Your strong-side winger is open on the wall.
opts: Shoulder check early, wheel the puck to the strong side, and make a firm wall pass
Force the reverse to your partner even though the inside lane is covered
Spin blind and fire the puck through the middle before pressure arrives
Hide behind the net until the forechecker leaves the inside lane
U15 / Bantam.explain: The forechecker has taken away the partner reverse, but that opens the strong side. Reading that early lets you protect the puck and hit the winger before the forecheck resets.
U15 / Bantam.tip: Take the outlet the forechecker gives you.

U15 / Bantam.sit: When you receive a pass in the offensive zone with no immediate pressure, one-touching it away right away is usually better than holding it long enough to draw a defender.
U15 / Bantam.tip: Use space to make defenders move.
U15 / Bantam.why: A quick touch can be right under pressure, but with time and space you can hold the puck, force a defender to commit, and open a better passing or shooting lane.

U15 / Bantam.sit: A forward enters the zone with speed on a 1-on-3. Instead of using the open perimeter ice to delay, they attack straight through all three defenders and lose the puck.
U15 / Bantam.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They failed to recognize they were outnumbered and did not delay for support
They stayed wide too long instead of cutting into the three defenders sooner
They looked for a late teammate instead of shooting from outside the blue line
They kept possession instead of dumping the puck the instant they crossed the line
U15 / Bantam.explain: On a 1-on-3, attacking the middle is low percentage. The better U15 read is to use the perimeter, delay, and let support arrive so the rush can become a connected attack.

U15 / Bantam.sit: Your team turns the puck over deep. The first forward back starts hard, then glides through the neutral zone while watching the puck behind them.
U15 / Bantam.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They stopped skating hard before recovering to the defensive house
They checked over their shoulder instead of staring only at their own net
They backchecked through the middle instead of veering off for a line change
They avoided reaching from behind and taking a penalty
U15 / Bantam.explain: A backcheck is not done when you can see the play. The first forward back has to keep skating through the middle until the dangerous ice is protected, then sort out the next threat.

U18 / Midget.sit: You are a defender pinching at the left point in the offensive zone. Your centre has the puck at the half-wall but is being angled hard into the corner. The opposing right winger is hovering near your blue line, and the opposing centre has begun drifting toward the neutral zone. The puck has not moved yet. Based on your read, what is your best adjustment?
opts: Pinch deeper into the corner and help your centre hold the puck there
Hold at the point and call for a pass from your centre under pressure
Jump to the net for a tip-in while your centre still controls the puck
Begin recovering to your defensive zone before the two opponents can spring their counter
U18 / Midget.explain: Two opponents are already setting up a counter before the puck even moves. Your centre being forced into the corner makes a turnover likely, and staying pinched leaves the winger near your blue line with a clear head start. Recovering now takes away that lane before any rush can develop.
